title: CHR maintains stance vs. abortion except in extreme cases
summary: CHR maintains stance vs abortion except in extreme cases

blocks.text: The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) on Thursday stood firm on its pro-life position, saying it opposes abortion except for when a woman's life is at risk, or if she is a rape victim, or there are medical grounds for the procedure.
This was brought up during the Senate plenary deliberations into the proposed P1.285-billion budget of the CHR for fiscal year 2027.
During the session, Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III asked the CHR of its current stand regarding abortion, considering that there have been efforts seeking to decriminalize it.

“The official stand of the Commission on Human Rights is pro-life. They are anti-abortion, except in extreme circumstances, for example, life-threatening, second, victims of rape, and medical reasons,” budget sponsor Senator JV Ejercito answered.
Sotto said he would no longer propound any more questions if the CHR is maintaining its position against abortion.

“Thank you for that because there is an ongoing hearing. I understand that they are trying to revise the Revised Penal Code. So, hearing that from the CHR, I have no more questions and I have no problem with the budget, Mr. President. I fully support the submission,” he said.
Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri, meanwhile, also welcomed CHR’s take.
Describing himself as a "Republican" conservative lawmaker, Zubiri said he is "pro-life."

“We appreciate the fact that you came out stating that you will not support legislation to that effect to decriminalize abortion because ayaw po nating mangyari katulad ng Estados Unidos na ano lang, parang pwede kang pumunta ng mall at magpa-abortion [we don’t want to be like the United States where people could just go to a mall and get an abortion],” he said.
“Over my dead body will I allow legislation to that effect, which shall allow decriminalizing of abortion while I’m here in the Senate,” he added.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) earlier maintained that abortion is a crime, but admitted that it was open to proposing exemptions with proposed amendments to the Revised Penal Code (RPC) pending before the House of Representatives.

A DOJ committee reportedly prepared a draft Criminal Code of the Philippines which aims to amend the RPC. A DOJ official also said there were efforts by some progressive lawmakers to decriminalize abortion. — BM, GMA News
